scqa.name: SCQA (Situation–Complication–Question–Answer)
scqa.summary: Barbara Minto's pyramid-principle arc: surface the recommendation up front, then layer key arguments and supporting evidence beneath it. The default for executive memos, strategic recommendations, and consulting decks where the audience needs the answer fast.

beats.name: Situation
beats.description: Establish the shared context: what is true today that the audience already agrees on. State only facts the audience accepts without argument. The goal is alignment, not persuasion — you are setting the stage.

beats.name: Complication
beats.description: Introduce the disturbance to the situation: what changed, what is at risk, what is no longer working. This is the tension that makes the audience lean in. Be specific and quantify the change where possible.

beats.name: Key Question
beats.description: Surface the question the complication forces the audience to answer. Frame it explicitly — 'Should we…?', 'How do we…?', 'What changes if…?'. The question should feel inevitable given the complication.

beats.name: Answer
beats.description: Deliver the recommendation in a single sentence, up front. No arguments yet, no caveats — just the conclusion the rest of the deck will defend. This is the apex of the Minto pyramid; everything that follows supports it.

beats.name: Key Arguments
beats.description: Lay out the two or three top-level reasons the answer is correct. One slide per argument, or one summary slide naming all of them. Each argument should stand alone as a compelling reason; together they should be exhaustive of the case.

beats.name: Supporting Evidence
beats.description: Present the data, examples, and case studies that ground each argument. Pyramid-principle style: every claim above is backed by something verifiable here. Cite sources; show the numbers; let the evidence carry the weight.

academic.name: Academic
academic.summary: Researchers, professors, and students expecting rigorous methodology, citations, and evidence-based conclusions.
academic.description: Researchers, professors, and students who expect rigorous methodology, citations, and evidence-based conclusions. Cite every source, show confidence intervals, be transparent about method, and leave marketing language out. Chart density can be high; 20-50 slides with time reserved for questions.

sell.name: Sell
sell.summary: Move a buyer or evaluator toward purchase, adoption, renewal, or expansion.
sell.description: Use for customer-facing decks where the goal is commercial movement. Focus on pain, value, proof, differentiation, and the next buying step.
sell.outcome: The buyer advances to the next step in the commercial process.
successCriteria: Value is tied to customer outcomes

formal.name: Formal
formal.summary: Polished, restrained voice for board, investor, and regulator audiences.
formal.description: Authoritative without being cold. Use third-person constructions, full sentences, and concrete numbers. Avoid hedges and humor that depend on shared in-jokes; rely on clarity and precision to land.
voiceCues: Use third person and the corporate 'we' sparingly.
Lead with the recommendation, then evidence.
Quote concrete numbers; avoid round-tripping ranges.
Prefer full sentences to bullet fragments on key claims.
samplePhrases: Q4 revenue grew 18% year over year, led by enterprise expansion.
We recommend approving the Series B raise at $30M.
Net retention was 124%; gross retention was 96%.

bold.name: Bold
bold.description: A vibrant, high-energy theme with bold colors and a dynamic, attention-grabbing style. Great for presentations that need to stand out.

pastel-red.name: Pastel Red
pastel-red.summary: Soft red and blue accents for approachable consumer stories.
pastel-red.description: A pastel red scheme with warm neutrals and blue support, suited to friendly, human-centered decks.

burnt-orange.name: Burnt Orange
burnt-orange.summary: Warm orange and red accents for energetic commercial decks.
burnt-orange.description: A warm, high-contrast palette built around burnt orange, red, navy, and gold. It feels active without losing structure.

tahoma.name: Tahoma
tahoma.description: Tahoma is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Tahoma for both headings and body text.

impact.name: Impact
impact.description: Impact is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Impact for headings with Grandview for body text.

title-subtitle.name: Title Subtitle
title-subtitle.summary: Reach for it when a headline needs one supporting line, as on a cover or a section opener.
title-subtitle.description: A title with a subtitle beneath it. Use it for the cover slide, for section openers, or for a closing slide with a headline and a short follow-up line.

text-3x.name: Text 3x
text-3x.summary: Reach for it when three parallel points each need a short passage of their own.
text-3x.description: A title above three text blocks in a row, equal in weight. Use it for three pillars, three steps explained in prose, or three options described one by one.

chart-3x.name: Chart 3x
chart-3x.summary: Reach for it when three charts tell one story, each with its own note.
chart-3x.description: A title above three charts, each followed by a text block, in three columns. Use it for a small-multiples view of three metrics, regions or cohorts.

list-3x.name: List 3x
list-3x.summary: Reach for it when three groups of points need their own lists.
list-3x.description: A title above three lists in a row. Use it for three themes, three phases or three audiences, each with a few bullets.
